clue.text: Instrument adjusted without tuning peg

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: to set something is to adjust it, as a clock or a dial
a pin is the peg round which a string is wound for tuning

explanation.surface: Someone retunes a keyboard instrument while one of its pegs is missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking, so the tuning peg is wrapped rather than removed.
explanation.definitionFit: A spinet is a small harpsichord-like keyboard, so it is a musical instrument.

clue.text: Performing a flop we get the bird

indicators.note: performing suggests the letters put on a show in a new order

explanation.surface: An act that fails on stage gets booed off: the performers 'get the bird'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Performing' rearranges A FLOP WE; 'get the bird' is British slang for being booed, but here the bird is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A peafowl, peacock or peahen, is a large pheasant-family species of bird.

clue.text: Darling pet, idiot granny

definitions.meaning: in Peter Pan the Darling family's pet dog and nursemaid is called ...
a child's word for a grandmother

explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions: the Darlings are the family in Peter Pan, whose dog-nurse has this name.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the dog in Peter Pan, British slang for a fool, and a nursery word for grandmother.

clue.text: A bit of track railmen laid out?

definitions.text: A bit of track railmen laid out?

indicators.note: a bit of the word track is just its opening letter
laid out suggests the letters are rearranged, as workers lay out rails

explanation.surface: Railway workers set out a section of rails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A bit of' takes T from track, and 'laid out' rearranges RAILMEN into RAMLINE; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tramline is one of the rails on which a tram runs, a piece of track that railmen lay.

clue.text: Prosecutor with pretence to be a silk

parts.note: DA is a District Attorney, a US public prosecutor
a mask is a false front or pretence

explanation.surface: A lawyer who prosecutes puts on a show of being a senior barrister.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a 'silk' is a senior barrister (a QC or KC), which makes the lawyer reading tempting; here it is the fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Damask is a figured woven fabric, traditionally made of silk.

clue.text: German person trying to lose weight

explanation.walkthrough: The German first name and the slimmer are spelt the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Dieter is a typical German forename, and anyone on a slimming regime is one who diets.

clue.text: What could yield essential ceramic

indicators.note: the letters of the two words could be made to yield something new when rearranged

explanation.surface: A field of study that might produce some vital ceramic substance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could yield' rearranges the sixteen letters of ESSENTIAL CERAMIC; the whole clue also describes the discipline that develops ceramics.
explanation.definitionFit: The engineering discipline studying metals, polymers and ceramics is the one that would produce a new ceramic.

clue.text: See 6
Strike breaker, a good idea

parts.note: to brain someone is to strike them on the head
a breaker is a wave breaking on the shore

explanation.surface: Someone breaking a strike thinks this is a clever plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strike breaker' suggests a scab crossing a picket line; it is really two pieces, a verb and a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A brainwave is a sudden clever inspiration.

clue.text: Bitterly cold officers mess

parts.note: the brass is slang for senior officers
to monkey with something is to mess about with it

explanation.surface: Senior officers' dining room, or a chaotic scene among them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mess' suggests an officers' mess, but here it is a verb; 'brass monkey' weather is British slang for freezing cold.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang calls freezing weather 'brass monkey' weather, from 'cold enough to freeze the balls off a brass monkey'.

clue.text: It is not commonly a blemish

parts.note: the dialect form '... starts with T standing for it
ain't is the common or non-standard form of is not

explanation.surface: A dialect speaker insists something is not a flaw.
explanation.walkthrough: The dialect contraction 'tain't (it ain't) is spelt the same as the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A taint is a stain or trace of corruption, a mark on something.

clue.text: Women willing to try a second portion of sweet

parts.note: to test is to try out
in a trice means in a second, an instant

indicators.note: a portion of the word sweet is just its first letter

explanation.surface: Ladies keen to sample a second helping of pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'willing' is not eager but making a will: testatrices are women who make wills. TRICE is an instant, so stands for 'second'.
explanation.definitionFit: Testatrices is the plural of testatrix, the legal term for a woman who leaves a will.

clue.text: Engaged in work on the 6, summit

parts.note: to be at something is to be engaged in it, as in 'at work'
op is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: Someone busy with a job at the top of a mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed '6,' is a scanning error; the clue reads 'on the summit'. OP (opus) is a standard abbreviation for a work.
explanation.definitionFit: Atop is a preposition meaning on top of, at the very peak.

clue.text: Models for obscene pictures

parts.note: blue means smutty or indecent, as in a blue film
prints are photographs or pictures

explanation.surface: Lewd photos used as templates for something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blue' for obscene is common British usage (blue jokes, blue films).
explanation.definitionFit: Blueprints are technical plans or patterns that serve as templates.

clue.text: Primary element of implant close in bust

definitions.text: Primary element of implant close in bust

indicators.note: bust means broken, so the letters are smashed and rearranged
the primary element of the word implant is its first letter

explanation.surface: Cosmetic surgery: the main material in a breast implant sits within the chest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bust' looks like the chest but signals breaking: I (first of implant) plus CLOSE IN are rearranged. The whole clue also describes the material.
explanation.definitionFit: Silicone gel is the polymer most often used to fill breast implants.

clue.text: Cheat has wits to go on and on

parts.note: a card is a witty or eccentric person
to harp on is to talk about something tediously

explanation.surface: A fraudster who is clever and keeps talking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'card' for a joker or wit is old British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A card-sharp is a swindler who cheats at card games.

clue.text: Space to host final of competition?

definitions.text: Space to host final of competition?

indicators.note: to host is to hold a guest, so one piece contains the other

parts.note: an area is a space or expanse

indicators.note: the final of the word competition is its last letter

explanation.surface: Looking for a venue big enough to stage a championship final.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to host' puts N, the last letter of competition, inside AREA; the whole clue also describes a stadium.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is an enclosed area for sports events, where a cup final may be staged.

clue.text: Support in chemists for illicit goods

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: Boots is a large British chain of chemists' shops
a leg is a support, as of a table

explanation.surface: Bottles of medicine at the pharmacy are really contraband.
explanation.walkthrough: Boots is a British high-street chemists' chain; 'Support' at the front of the clue is the piece put inside, not the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Bootlegs are smuggled or illegally made goods, originally liquor hidden in boot tops.

clue.text: One revealing gay exterior

definitions.meaning: someone who exposes a person's homosexuality, 'outs' them

explanation.walkthrough: One sense is the noun from the verb 'to out' someone, the other the adjective for outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who publicly exposes another's sexuality outs them; and the word also means outside or external.

clue.text: Stick with Dodd, finally youthful in heart

indicators.note: in places the letter inside the other piece

parts.note: ticker is slang for the heart

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of youthful

explanation.surface: A comedian's prop, and a heart that stays young at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: Ken Dodd was a British comedian famous for waving a 'tickling stick', a feather duster; L (last of youthful) goes in TICKER.
explanation.definitionFit: Ken Dodd's tickling stick was his trademark prop, a feather duster for tickling.

clue.text: Gear Moss modelled is very flimsy

indicators.note: modelled means shaped into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Kate Moss's catwalk clothes are extremely light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moss' suggests the model Kate Moss, but it is anagram fodder with GEAR, and 'modelled' is the anagram indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Gossamer is fine cobweb thread, so as an adjective it means delicately thin and light.

clue.text: Being ill, one is taken in by man

indicators.note: taken in by means held inside the following piece

parts.note: a male is a man
a, the indefinite article, means one

explanation.surface: A man deceives someone who is unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in' suggests deceived, but it is a container signal; 'Being ill' is a noun phrase, matching the noun answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Malaise is a general feeling of being unwell or uneasy.

clue.text: That is upstanding person, see

indicators.note: in a down clue, upstanding means the word is read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: a man is a person
Ely is a cathedral city, so a bishop's see

explanation.surface: A respectable person tells you to look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see' is not look but a bishop's diocese; Ely is the crossword's favourite see.
explanation.definitionFit: Namely introduces an explanation, like i.e., meaning 'specifically' or 'to wit'.

clue.text: Gets off with loose women after excitement

indicators.note: after places one piece behind the other

parts.note: kicks are thrills or excitement
tarts is slang for promiscuous women

explanation.surface: Someone pulls promiscuous partners once they've had their thrills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets off with' suggests a sexual encounter; 'Gets off' alone is the definition, starting something going.
explanation.definitionFit: Kick-starts means starts off or gets going, as an engine or a project.

clue.text: Horse turned round left group

indicators.note: round means placed around the other piece
turned means the word is reversed

parts.note: a cob is a sturdy short-legged horse

explanation.surface: A rider turns their horse and leaves the herd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses COB to BOC, and 'round' puts it around L.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloc is an alliance of countries or parties acting as a group.

clue.text: Exchange prisoners heading north

indicators.note: in a down clue heading north means read upwards

parts.note: POWs are prisoners of war

explanation.surface: Prisoners being swapped as they travel north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading north' reverses POWS in a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Swop is a variant spelling of swap, to trade one thing for another.

clue.text: Where war leaders met to locate retreating army

indicators.note: retreating means the word goes backwards

parts.note: to lay is to put or locate something
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve force

explanation.surface: Wartime leaders' summit spot, where the army is found pulling back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreating' reverses LAY to YAL; the TA is Britain's Territorial Army.
explanation.definitionFit: Churchill, Roosevelt and Stalin held their 1945 conference at the Crimean resort, so it is a summit venue.

clue.text: In unruly weeds lies flower

indicators.note: unruly suggests letters out of order

explanation.surface: An Alpine bloom lies among overgrown weeds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unruly' rearranges WEEDS LIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Edelweiss is a white Alpine plant with woolly bracts.

clue.text: Goes down with unknown disease

parts.note: drops means falls or goes down
y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: Someone falls ill with a mystery ailment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goes down with' tempts as catching an illness; Y is an algebraic unknown.
explanation.definitionFit: Dropsy is an old name for oedema, swelling from fluid build-up, a medical condition.

clue.text: A fool for every engineer

parts.note: a sap is a gullible fool
per means for each

explanation.surface: Every engineer is considered an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: A sapper is a soldier in the Royal Engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapper is the rank and nickname of a private in the British Army's Royal Engineers.
